 Liverpool and Chelsea clash in battle of the Basques and Man City continue defence - Carabao Cup talking points 
 Watch every match from the Carabao Cup fourth round live on Sky Sports; watch in-game clips and FREE match highlights across Sky Sports' digital platforms; Watch Liverpool vs Chelsea live on Sky Sports Main Event on Wednesday
 Wednesday 28 October 2026 18:39, UK
 Image: 
 English teenagers Reggie Watson and Rio Ngumoha turned out for Chelsea and Liverpool in their respective Carabao Cup third-round victories
 In the battle of the Basques, how strong will Iraola and Alonso go?
 Liverpool vs Chelsea - Wednesday, kick-off 8pm live on Sky Sports Main Event 
 It will be intriguing to see how strong Andoni Iraola and Xabi Alonso go with their line-ups at Anfield on Wednesday night, with both Basque managers facing crucial Premier League fixtures at the weekend, albeit for different reasons.
 Liverpool are in the midst of a four-game run at Anfield and will head into the Chelsea clash buoyed by three consecutive wins. Will the Reds' head coach prioritise the visit of reigning champions Arsenal on Super Sunday , or could another victory help sustain the feel-good factor around the club?
 Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player
 Highlights of the Carabao Cup match between Liverpool and Tottenham. 
 Either way, one player certain to feature against the club where he began his career is young Reds forward Rio Ngumoha, who impressed against Villarreal in the Champions League last week before playing the final 13 minutes of Sunday's 2-0 win over Brighton.
 As for the visitors, Alonso will be looking for a response from his players after Saturday's "awful" 2-0 defeat to Tottenham, as Gary Neville described Chelsea's performance at the Stamford Bridge. However, with crucial league fixtures against Man Utd, Sunderland and Leeds on the horizon, where will the Chelsea manager's priorities lie?
 Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player
 Highlights from the Carabao Cup match between Chelsea and Leeds. 
 Alonso, who will be without the suspended Cole Palmer following his sending-off against Spurs, will surely be keen to freshen things up at Anfield. However, as Paul Merson warned on Sky Sports, Chelsea cannot afford to take their eye off the league, with two damaging defeats potentially putting their Champions League hopes at risk.
 "If they get beat by Liverpool and Man Utd this week, then Chelsea are in big trouble. You'd be seriously thinking they'd be lucky to get Champions League this season. And that can't happen. Whatever happens, that can't happen."
 Rich Morgan 
 Liverpool 
 Chelsea
 Wednesday 28th October 7:00pm
 Kick off 8:00pm
 Man City-Brighton double-header presents big chance for Hurzeler
 Man City vs Brighton - Wednesday, kick-off 7.30pm live on Sky Sports+ 
 Manchester City and Brighton meet twice this week, once in the cup and once in the league. It's a chance for Fabian Hurzeler to prove that Brighton can consistently mix it with the best teams in the division after faltering at Liverpool at the weekend.
 Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player
 Highlights of the third round Carabao Cup match between Man City and Norwich City. 
 For all the club's progress, and the never-ending stream of compliments about Hurzeler's progressive style of play, he is missing the tangible evidence to cement Brighton as the Premier League's great disruptors. The EFL Cup presents the perfect opportunity to do that.
 Brighton are unbeaten in four games against Man City (W2, D2) - their best ever run against such usually-dominant opposition. Hurzeler's brand of high-intensity football is exactly the style City tend to find most unsettling, so the visitors should arrive to the Etihad full of confidence.
 They're perfectly capable of causing an upset to dispatch of the holders.
 Laura Hunter 
 Europe has helped, not hindered - but can Villa and Bournemouth also balance cup run?
 Bournemouth vs Aston Villa - Wednesday, kick-off 7.45pm live on Sky Sports+ 
 Europe is usually viewed as a hindrance to domestic form, but it has been a positive thus far for Aston Villa and Bournemouth.
 Both teams started slowly this season. Villa had not scored a goal in the Premier League until the 2-1 defeat to Nottingham Forest on September 12, while their first league win came a week later at Tottenham.
 Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player
 FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Aston Villa and Manchester City. 
 Unai Emery's men kicked into gear with a 3-2 win against Club Brugge earlier in September and have now gone seven games unbeaten across all competitions since beating Coventry City in the last round of the Carabao Cup.
 Bournemouth are a similar story. It was a slow start under Marco Rose, but their performances in the Europa League have ignited the new era.
 They had to wait until October 18 for a first win in the top flight but they now come into this game against Villa full of confidence after beating AC Milan and Manchester United across a four-game winning streak.
 Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player
 FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from Manchester United’s match against Bournemouth in the Premier League. 
 After starting slowly, the two teams are beginning to flex their muscles and are showcasing why they are regarded as two of the best run clubs in the division. However, how they balance this Carabao Cup tie will be the ultimate test for their squad depth.
 Can they juggle European football, the priority that is the Premier League and a cup run? We'll find out on Wednesday.
 Patrick Rowe 
 Fulham finding form as Palace and Sage face Carabao Cup reckoning
 Fulham vs Crystal Palace - Wednesday, kick-off 7.45pm live on Sky Sports+ 
 When Fulham and Crystal Palace first met in early September, both managers were under pressure after losing their opening two Premier League games. Ahead of Wednesday's Carabao Cup meeting, however, the balance of power has shifted dramatically.
 Alvaro Arbeloa's Fulham have found momentum at precisely the right time, winning back-to-back league games against Hull and Coventry.
 Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player
 FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from Fulham’s match against Crystal Palace in the Premier League. 
 Oscar Bobb's late winner at the CBS Arena was another sign of a side growing in resilience, while consecutive clean sheets suggest they are beginning to find the defensive stability that eluded them earlier in the season.
 The crisis has not disappeared, but Arbeloa has bought himself breathing room via 'Arbeloa-ball'.
 Pierre Sage, meanwhile, is facing an altogether different reckoning at Palace.
 Consecutive defeats to Brighton and Newcastle, conceding seven goals without reply, have exposed a team desperately short of defensive organisation and confidence.
 Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player
 Take a look at some of the future Premier League stars making their mark in the third round of the Carabao Cup. 
 Palace have shipped 19 league goals, the division's worst record, and Sage's insistence that the problems are not tactical will do little to silence the growing discontent among supporters.
 Wednesday offers Fulham a chance to deepen Palace's crisis. For Sage, it risks becoming another step towards the exit.
 William Bitibiri 
 Can the Bees make it three in a row?
 Sunderland vs Brentford - Wednesday, kick-off 7.45pm live on Sky Sports+ 
 Given their contrasting form this season, Brentford will be confident heading to the Stadium of Light this week. Not only that, they also have a decent pedigree in recent Carabao Cup campaigns.
 Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player
 FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from Hull City’s match against Brentford in the Premier League. 
 They have reached the quarter-finals in three of the last five seasons, including the last two - and were knocked out by the eventual winners in 2024/25 (Newcastle) and 2025/26 (Man City). Finalists Chelsea knocked them out in their other quarter-final appearance in 2021/22.
 Of course, Keith Andrews will be hoping to go one better this season - but they have Sunderland to beat first.
 The Black Cats have been eliminated in six of their last eight League Cup fourth round ties - the most recent in 2021/22 - and are struggling to find the magic touch they had last season.
 Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player
 FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Sunderland and Leeds United. 
 But form doesn't always translate onto the pitch and knockout football is a different beast altogether. At home, Sunderland will feel they are a match for anyone - and will not want to get stung again on Wednesday.
 Charlotte Marsh 
 Can Toffees or Magpies lay down a marker before PL rematch? 
 Everton vs Newcastle - Thursday, kick-off 7.45pm live on Sky Sports+ 
 The Carabao Cup often gives teams a chance to rotate their squad in order to remain fresh for the upcoming Premier League games. That is less likely to be the case here. Instead, it could act as a preview of their league meeting on Monday night.
 Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player
 Highlights from the Premier League match between Arsenal and Everton. 
 Everton’s paper-thin squad has already been rocked by the illness of Jack Grealish and the concussion of Jarrad Branthwaite. Whether he likes it or not, David Moyes will have to go to the well with the exact same group and just pray for no more knocks.
 Newcastle’s options have also been rather depleted, but they do have the advantage when it comes to strength in depth, aided greatly by the return of Anthony Elanga during the league win over Crystal Palace.
 Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player
 FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Crystal Palace and Newcastle United. 
 The thirst for silverware on Tyneside may encourage Matthias Jaissle to put out a relatively strong team as the Magpies look to regain the title they won two years' ago under Eddie Howe.
 If these two do line up strongly, then perhaps as important as progression in the cup is the opportunity to lay down a marker before they meet again on Merseyside a mere 96 hours later.
 Callum Bishop
